claims.statement: `app/api/webhooks/clerk/route.ts` has no session to check because Clerk is the caller, so it authenticates the request by verifying the body signature with Clerk's `verifyWebhook()` against `CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET` and answers 400 on failure; no `proxy.ts` exclusion is necessary because the middleware matcher already covers `/api(.*)` and only stamps `x-pathname`.

`requireAuthenticatedUser()` lives in `modules/auth/data/auth.ts` — a `data/` layer that is private to its module — so only `app/` may call it, and the only two callers are the `(dashboard)` layout's first statement and `app/api-docs/page.tsx`, which sits outside the route group; a route outside `(dashboard)` stays unauthenticated until it adds its own call.

A signed-in user with no `profiles` row has no role: `getAuthUserId()` still returns an id and an inactive profile still resolves for the layout, but `current_profile_id()` returns NULL so every RLS predicate fails and reads return zero rows — which is why deactivation is not a sign-out and why a fresh sign-up reads as an empty dashboard.

`user.updated` routes back through `upsertProfileFromClerkUser`, whose existing-profile path re-attempts the invitation membership insert; without it a membership insert that failed on `user.created` would be permanent because the webhook still answered 200 and Clerk never retried.

Provisioning runs only on the service-role client because no Clerk session exists for `user.created`/`user.deleted`, making the Clerk webhook route the sole sanctioned `service_role` path (rule 3); a throw becomes a 500 so Clerk retries, and any future caller outside that route would be running with RLS bypassed.

`app/sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx` has no screen of its own: it redirects to `/sign-in?sign_up=1`, which opens the `SignUpModal` island from the sign-in card; the modal deliberately does not activate the new session because an administrator must still assign school and role.

`sanitizeRedirectUrl` closes the open-redirect failure — signing in against the real app and then being handed to an attacker's site — by rejecting every form the browser resolves off-site: an absolute URL, a protocol-relative `//host`, a backslash after the leading slash, and a `javascript:`/`data:` scheme; the sanitized value is both the signed-in destination and the `redirectUrl` given to Clerk's OAuth start, so there is one place to get it right.

`session_exists` — Clerk's 400 when a sign-in is started while the browser already holds a session — is handled by `isSessionExistsError` scanning `errors[]` for that code and returning false for a bare `Error`, `null` or an empty array; the sign-in card checks it at six handlers (password, MFA, device verification, Google SSO, account create, submit) and each calls `continueExistingSession()` instead of showing an error, so a user who is in fact signed in is never blocked by a red card.

`startGoogleSignIn` must await a `reset()` before calling `sso()` whenever `signIn.status` is non-null, because `sso()` silently declines to start an attempt when it sees a stale status and surfaces no error; the unit test models `status` as a mutable field cleared only when the delayed `reset()` resolves, so an un-awaited reset fails the test the way it failed in production.

The invitation membership split narrows the never-re-grant invariant rather than holding it whole: `upsertProfileFromClerkUser` calls `ensureTenantMembership` on the update path too, so a membership is written only when the profile holds none — a grant can never add a second school or move someone an admin has already placed, while an admin authoring a grant onto an existing tenantless user through Clerk's Backend API is applied at the next delivery.

`app/api/openapi.json/route.ts` uses `getAuthUserId()` and answers 401 instead of redirecting, the softer variant of the gate reserved for machine callers; swapping it into a Server Component would let the tree render before the gate resolves.

`requireAuthenticatedUser()` is the one hard gate and has exactly two callers — `app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` as its first statement and `app/api-docs/page.tsx`, which sits outside the route group — while every other consumer (dashboard `tenant-scope.ts` and `tenant-access.ts`, `/schools/new`, `/users/new`, billing, report, the sign-in layout, `/api/openapi.json`) uses the soft `getAuthUserId()` and handles `null` itself, so a rendering Server Component must hard-redirect and an identity-to-status caller must not.

A rendering page cannot own its own gate from a module: `modules/<domain>/data/` is private (rule 8) and only `app/` may fetch from it, so a `modules/x/ui` page stays ungated unless its `app/` route calls `requireAuthenticatedUser`, and the gate returning an id rather than a profile leaves the profile read separate and fallible.

`lib/supabase/service.ts` is deliberately the only reader of `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` and throws when it or the Supabase URL is missing rather than falling back to `anon`, because a silent anon fallback would surface as a much less obvious RLS write failure; the module therefore owns the whole no-session surface and a new `provisioning.ts` caller outside the webhook is a security change, not a refactor.

`ensure_profile_tenant_membership` takes a `for update` lock on the profile row and returns early when any membership exists, making the check-then-insert one serialization point per profile; because the lock is held, a duplicate-key `23505` can only come from a writer outside the helper and is accepted, while any other error is logged and rethrown, and the function is executable by `service_role` alone so RLS never applies to the call.

The rethrow behind membership failure is load-bearing: a swallowed error leaves a signed-in Clerk user with no profile row, hence a `null` role, failing predicates and an empty dashboard, so the webhook answers 500 and hands the problem to Clerk's retry.

`data/provisioning.ts` selects the profile by `clerk_user_id` and branches: the insert path writes `role: grant?.role ?? 'viewer'` with `is_active: true`, while the update path touches only `full_name` and `email` and then repairs a membership only when a grant parses — so the never-re-grant invariant is narrowed rather than held whole, and a tenantless profile an admin rescues through Clerk's Backend API still gets seated.

The invitation branch's trusted-metadata argument depends on an admin gate that is not RLS: `inviteUser` writes to Clerk, which sees no Postgres policy, so `authorizeAdminCaller` resolves the caller's profile and checks `resolveTrustedRole` against `'admin'` before the invitation branch, never `resolveRouteRole` whose `?role=` override would let any signed-in user claim admin.

`inviteUser` keeps Clerk's `ignoreExisting` at its default so a second invitation for one address is reported as `duplicate` instead of created, because two live invitations with different grants would let which link a person clicks decide their access.

Only two places hard-redirect at all: the `(dashboard)` layout gates, and the sign-in layout redirects `/` when a session already exists, while `app/sign-up/[[...sign-up]]/page.tsx` owns no screen and forwards to `/sign-in?sign_up=1`, which seeds the modal's open state.

`sanitizeRedirectUrl` trims surrounding whitespace and accepts only values that already start with a single slash, so a bare hostname like `evil.com` or `dashboard` also falls back to `/` alongside the scheme, protocol-relative and backslash traps.

`SignUpModal` completes `attemptEmailAddressVerification` into a `done` step without calling `setActive()`, deliberately leaving the session inactive because an administrator must still assign the new profile's school and role.

`resolveTrustedRole` reads only the DB column it is handed, with no Clerk `publicMetadata` fallback, because the dashboard once read the metadata while the sidebar read the database and showed one admin as `ADMIN` and `VIEWER` on the same screen (audit I5); `resolveRouteRole`/`resolveDisplayRole`/`toOfficeRole` layer a `?role=` preview on top so a caller can preview up, and their least-privileged fallback is read-only `viewer`, never a write-enabled variant.
